units.zh: 于洛侯 胡泥 李洪之 子神 張赦提 趙霸 崔暹 邸珍 田式 燕榮 元弘嗣 王文同
units.en: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Zi Shen, Zhang Sheti, Zhao Ba, Cui Xuan, Di Zhen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Yuan Hongsi, and Wang Wentong
units.literal: Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Zi Shen, Zhang Sheti, Zhao Ba, Cui Xuan, Di Zhen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Yuan Hongsi, Wang Wentong

units.zh: 夫為國之體有四焉：一曰仁義，二曰禮制，三曰法令，四曰刑罰。
units.en: The foundation of statecraft rests on four pillars: humanity and righteousness, ritual institutions, laws and decrees, and punishments.
units.literal: The structure of governing a state has four elements: first, humanity and righteousness; second, ritual institutions; third, laws and decrees; fourth, punishments and penalties.

units.zh: 仁義、禮制，教之本也；
units.en: Humanity, righteousness, and ritual are the roots of civilizing instruction;
units.literal: Humanity, righteousness, and ritual institutions are the root of instruction;

units.zh: 法令、刑罰，教之末也。
units.en: while laws, decrees, and punishments are its branches.
units.literal: Laws, decrees, punishments, and penalties are the branch of instruction.

units.zh: 無本不立，無末不成。
units.en: Without roots nothing stands; without branches nothing is complete.
units.literal: Without the root nothing can stand; without the branch nothing can be completed.

units.zh: 然教化遠而刑罰近，可以助化而不可以專行，可以立威而不可以繁用。
units.en: Moral transformation works slowly and from afar, whereas punishment operates at close hand. Punishment may aid civilizing effort but cannot replace it; it may inspire awe but must not be wielded constantly.
units.literal: Yet civilizing influence is distant while punishments are near—they can assist in transformation but cannot be applied exclusively; they can establish awe but cannot be used frequently.

units.zh: 老子曰：「其政察察，其人缺缺。」
units.en: Laozi said, "When government is excessively exacting, the people grow impoverished in spirit."
units.literal: Laozi said: "When government is minutely scrutinizing, the people are deficient and incomplete."

units.zh: 又曰：「法令滋章，盜賊多有。」
units.en: He also said, "When laws and statutes proliferate, thieves and bandits multiply."
units.literal: He also said: "When laws and decrees multiply, robbers and bandits abound."

units.zh: 然則，令之煩苛，吏之嚴酷，不可致化，百世可知。
units.en: When ordinances grow burdensome and officials grow harsh, true transformation becomes impossible—a lesson clear for a hundred generations.
units.literal: Thus when ordinances are vexatious and officials severe and cruel, transformation cannot be achieved—this can be known for a hundred generations.

units.zh: 考覽前載，有時而用之矣。
units.en: A review of earlier histories shows that such methods have nevertheless been employed from time to time.
units.literal: Examining previous records, there have been times when such methods were employed.

units.zh: 昔秦任獄吏，赭衣滿道。
units.en: In antiquity the Qin state relied on prison officials, until the roads swarmed with convicts in ochre robes.
units.literal: In former times Qin employed prison clerks, and convicts in ochre garments filled the roads.

units.zh: 漢革其風，矯枉過正，禁綱疏闊，遂漏吞舟。
units.en: The Han reformed that harshness but overcorrected: the prohibitory net grew so slack that even great offenders slipped through.
units.literal: Han reformed this trend, correcting the crooked by over-straightening—the prohibitory net became loose and wide, until it let through those who could swallow a boat.

units.zh: 故大奸巨猾，犯義悖禮。
units.en: Great villains and cunning schemers therefore violated righteousness and defied ritual propriety.
units.literal: Thus great traitors and cunning villains violated righteousness and defied ritual.

units.zh: 郅都、甯成之倫，猛氣奮發，摧拉凶邪，一切以救時弊。
units.en: Men such as Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, fierce in spirit, crushed the wicked by every means solely to remedy the disorders of their age.
units.literal: Men like Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, with fierce energy flourishing, crushed and pulled down the wicked—everything solely to remedy the ills of the times.

units.zh: 雖乖教義，或有所取焉。
units.en: Though their methods ran counter to true civilizing doctrine, in certain respects something could still be learned from them.
units.literal: Though contrary to the doctrine of instruction, in certain respects there was something to be gained from them.

units.zh: 于洛侯之徒，前書編之《酷吏》。
units.en: Men such as Yu Luohou and his kind were recorded in earlier histories under the title "Cruel Officials."
units.literal: Men like Yu Luohou and his ilk were compiled in the earlier histories under "Cruel Officials."

units.zh: 或因餘緒，或以微功，遭遇時來，忝竊高位。
units.en: Some rose on lingering family influence, others on trifling merit; seizing a favorable moment, they presumptuously occupied high office.
units.literal: Some rode on remaining momentum, others won advancement through minor merit; encountering the opportune moment, they presumptuously usurped high position.

units.zh: 肆其褊性，多行無禮，君子小人，咸罹其毒。
units.en: They indulged their narrow tempers, acted without propriety, and whether gentleman or commoner, all suffered their harm.
units.literal: They gave full rein to their narrow natures, frequently acting without propriety—gentlemen and petty men alike suffered their poison.

units.zh: 凡所蒞職，莫不懍然。
units.en: Wherever they held office, everyone trembled before them.
units.literal: Wherever they took office, none failed to be in dread.

units.zh: 居其下者，視之如蛇虺；
units.en: Those beneath them looked on them as serpents and vipers;
units.literal: Those beneath them regarded them as serpents and vipers;

units.zh: 過其境者，逃之如寇仇。
units.en: and those who passed through their jurisdictions fled as from mortal enemies.
units.literal: those who passed through their territory fled as from bandit enemies.

units.zh: 與人之恩，心非好善；
units.en: When they showed favor, their hearts held no love of goodness;
units.literal: When they showed kindness to others, in their hearts it was not from love of goodness;

units.zh: 加人之罪，事非疾惡。
units.en: when they piled on guilt, it was not from zeal against evil.
units.literal: when they added crimes to others, in the matter it was not from hatred of evil.

units.zh: 其所笞辱，多在無辜。
units.en: Those they flogged and humiliated were mostly innocent.
units.literal: Those they flogged and humiliated were mostly the innocent.

units.zh: 察其所為，豺狼之不若也。
units.en: Judged by their deeds, they were worse than wolves and jackals.
units.literal: Observing their conduct, they were not equal to wolves and jackals.

units.zh: 其禁奸除猾，殆與郅、寧之倫異乎。
units.en: Their suppression of treachery and elimination of villains was rather different from the likes of Zhi Du and Ning Cheng, was it not?
units.literal: Their suppression of treachery and elimination of cunning—this differed little from the class of Zhi and Ning.

units.zh: 君子賤之，故編於《酷吏》。
units.en: Men of principle despised them; hence they are gathered in this chapter on cruel officials.
units.literal: Gentlemen despised them; therefore they are compiled in "Cruel Officials."

units.zh: 魏有于洛侯、胡泥、李洪之、高遵、張赦提、羊祉、崔暹、酈道元、穀楷。
units.en: Among the Wei were Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xuan, Li Daoyuan, and Gu Kai.
units.literal: Wei had Yu Luohou, Hu Ni, Li Hongzhi, Gao Zun, Zhang Sheti, Yang Zhi, Cui Xuan, Li Daoyuan, and Gu Kai.

units.zh: 齊有邸珍、宋游道、盧斐、畢義云。
units.en: Among the Qi were Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, and Bi Yiyun.
units.literal: Qi had Di Zhen, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, and Bi Yiyun.

units.zh: 《周書》不立此篇。
units.en: The History of Zhou contains no such chapter.
units.literal: The History of Zhou does not establish this section.

units.zh: 《隋書》有庫狄士文、田式、燕榮、趙仲卿、崔弘度、元弘嗣、王文同。
units.en: The History of Sui records Ku Di Shiwen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Zhao Zhongqing, Cui Hongdu, Yuan Hongsi, and Wang Wentong.
units.literal: The History of Sui has Ku Di Shiwen, Tian Shi, Yan Rong, Zhao Zhongqing, Cui Hongdu, Yuan Hongsi, and Wang Wentong.

units.zh: 今檢高遵、羊祉、酈道元、谷楷、宋游道、盧斐、畢義雲、庫狄士文、趙仲卿、崔弘度各從其家傳，其餘並列於此云。
units.en: In this compilation Gao Zun, Yang Zhi, Li Daoyuan, Gu Kai, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, Bi Yiyun, Ku Di Shiwen, Zhao Zhongqing, and Cui Hongdu are each treated in their family biographies; the rest are gathered here.
units.literal: Now examining this account: Gao Zun, Yang Zhi, Li Daoyuan, Gu Kai, Song Youdao, Lu Fei, Bi Yiyun, Ku Di Shiwen, Zhao Zhongqing, and Cui Hongdu each follow their family biographies; the remainder are all listed together here.

units.zh: 于洛侯
units.en: Yu Luohou
units.literal: Yu Luohou

units.zh: 于洛侯，代人也。
units.en: Yu Luohou was a native of Dai.
units.literal: Yu Luohou was a man of Dai.

units.zh: 為秦州刺史，貪酷安忍。
units.en: As governor of Qin Province he was greedy, brutal, and calmly cruel.
units.literal: As governor of Qinzhou he was greedy, cruel, and calmly cruel.

units.zh: 部人富熾奪人呂勝脛纏一具，洛侯輒鞭富熾一百，截其右腕。
units.en: When a local man named Fu Chi seized a pair of leg wrappings from Lü Sheng, Luohou had Fu Chi flogged one hundred strokes and his right wrist cut off.
units.literal: A man of the district, Fu Chi, seized from a man named Lü Sheng a pair of leg wrappings; Luohou immediately flogged Fu Chi one hundred times and cut off his right wrist.

units.zh: 百姓王隴客刺殺人王羌奴、王愈二人，依律罪死。
units.en: A commoner named Wang Longke had stabbed and killed Wang Qiannu and Wang Yu; by law he deserved death.
units.literal: The commoner Wang Longke had stabbed and killed Wang Qiannu and Wang Yu; according to the law the crime merited death.

units.zh: 而洛侯生拔隴客舌，刺其本，並刺胸腹二十餘瘡。
units.en: Yet Luohou tore out Longke's tongue while he was still alive, stabbed its root, and drove more than twenty blades into his chest and belly.
units.literal: Yet Luohou pulled out Longke's tongue while he was alive, stabbed its root, and together stabbed more than twenty wounds in chest and belly.

units.zh: 隴客不堪苦痛，隨刀戰動。
units.en: Longke could not endure the pain; with each cut his body jerked in agony.
units.literal: Longke could not bear the agony; at each stroke of the knife he convulsed.

units.zh: 乃立四柱，磔其手足。
units.en: Luohou then erected four posts and dismembered his limbs.
units.literal: Then he erected four posts and dismembered his hands and feet.

units.zh: 命將絕，始斬其首，支解四體，分懸道路。
units.en: Only when Longke was near death did Luohou behead him, quarter the body, and hang the pieces along the roads.
units.literal: When he was near death he at last beheaded him, dismembered the four limbs, and hung the pieces along the roads.

units.zh: 見者無不傷楚歎愕。
units.en: All who witnessed it were stricken with grief and horror.
units.literal: None who saw it failed to be wounded in heart, sighing in shock.

units.zh: 百姓王元壽等一時反叛。
units.en: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rose in rebellion at once.
units.literal: The commoners Wang Yuanshou and others rebelled all at once.

units.zh: 有司糾劾，孝文詔使者於州常刑人處，宣告兵人，然後斬洛侯以謝百姓。
units.en: The authorities impeached him. Emperor Xiaowen ordered an envoy to proclaim Luohou's crimes at the usual execution ground before the troops, then beheaded him to appease the people.
units.literal: The authorities impeached him; Emperor Xiaowen ordered an envoy at the place in the province where criminals were customarily executed to proclaim it to the soldiers, and then beheaded Luohou to appease the people.

units.zh: 胡泥，代人也。
units.en: Hu Ni was a native of Dai.
units.literal: Hu Ni was a man of Dai.

units.zh: 曆官至司衛監，賜爵永成侯。
units.en: He rose to Director of the Palace Guards and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng.
units.literal: He rose through offices to Director of the Palace Guards and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yongcheng.

units.zh: 泥率勒禁中，不憚豪貴。
units.en: Ni commanded the inner palace and did not shrink before the powerful and noble.
units.literal: Ni led and controlled the inner palace, not fearing the powerful and noble.

units.zh: 殿中尚書叔孫侯頭應內直而闕於一時，泥以法繩之。
units.en: When Shusun Houtou, Palace Minister, was briefly derelict in his inner duty, Ni punished him according to law.
units.literal: Shusun Houtou, Palace Minister, had been derelict for a moment in his inner duty; Ni applied the law to restrain him.

units.zh: 侯頭恃寵，遂與口諍。
units.en: Hou relied on imperial favor and quarreled with him openly.
units.literal: Hou relied on favor and thus quarreled with him in words.

units.zh: 孝文聞而嘉焉，賜泥衣服一襲，出為幽州刺史，假范陽。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowen heard of this and commended Ni, bestowing a suit of robes on him and appointing him governor of You Province with acting authority over Fanyang.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowen heard and commended this, bestowing on Ni one suit of clothes; he was sent out as governor of Youzhou with acting authority over Fanyang.

units.zh: 以北平陽尼碩學，遂表薦之。
units.en: Because Yang Ni of Beiping was a distinguished scholar, Ni recommended him in a memorial.
units.literal: Because Yang Ni of Beiping was learned in scholarship, he submitted a memorial recommending him.

units.zh: 轉為定州刺史。
units.en: He was later transferred to governor of Ding Province.
units.literal: He was transferred to governor of Dingzhou.

units.zh: 以暴虐，刑罰酷濫，受納貨賄，徽還戮之。
units.en: For brutality, excessive punishments, and taking bribes, he was recalled and executed.
units.literal: For brutality and the excessive harshness of punishments, and for accepting bribes, he was summoned back and executed.

units.zh: 將就法，孝文臨太華殿引見，遣侍臣宣詔責之，遂就家賜盡。
units.en: As he was about to be executed, Emperor Xiaowen received him at Taihua Palace, sent an attendant to read an edict rebuking him, and then allowed him to take his own life at home.
units.literal: When he was about to suffer the law, Emperor Xiaowen came to the Taihua Palace to receive him in audience, sent an attendant to proclaim an edict reprimanding him, and then at his home granted him death.

units.zh: 李洪之
units.en: Li Hongzhi
units.literal: Li Hongzhi

units.zh: 李洪之，本名文通，恆農人也。
units.en: Li Hongzhi, whose original name was Wentong, was a native of Hengnong.
units.literal: Li Hongzhi, original name Wentong, was a man of Hengnong.

units.zh: 少為沙門，晚乃還俗。
units.en: In youth he was a Buddhist monk; only later did he return to lay life.
units.literal: In youth he was a monk; only in later years did he return to lay life.

units.zh: 真君中，為狄道護軍，賜爵安陽男。
units.en: During the Zhenjun reign he served as Protector-General of Didao and was enfeoffed as Baron of Anyang.
units.literal: In the Zhenjun era he was Protector-General of Didao and was granted the noble rank of Baron of Anyang.

units.zh: 會永昌王仁隨太武南征，得元後姊妹二人，洪之潛相餉遺，結為兄弟，遂便如親。
units.en: When Prince Yongchang Ren accompanied Emperor Taiwu on the southern campaign, he obtained two sisters of Empress Yuan. Hongzhi secretly sent them gifts, swore brotherhood with them, and thereafter treated them as kin.
units.literal: It happened that the Prince of Yongchang, Ren, accompanied Emperor Taiwu on the southern campaign and obtained two sisters of the Empress Yuan; Hongzhi secretly sent them gifts, entered brotherhood with them, and thereafter they were as close as kin.

units.zh: 頗得元後在南兄弟名字，乃改名洪之。
units.en: Learning the names of Empress Yuan's brothers in the south, he changed his own name to Hongzhi.
units.literal: He obtained rather fully the names of the Empress Yuan's brothers in the south, and thereupon changed his name to Hongzhi.

units.zh: 及仁坐事誅，元後入宮，得幸於文成，生獻文。
units.en: When Ren was executed for his crimes, Empress Yuan entered the palace, won favor from Emperor Wencheng, and bore Emperor Xianwen.
units.literal: When Ren was executed for his crime, the Empress Yuan entered the palace and won favor from Emperor Wencheng, bearing Emperor Xianwen.

units.zh: 元後臨崩，太后問其親，因言洪之為兄。
units.en: As Empress Yuan lay dying, the empress dowager asked about her kin; she said Hongzhi was her brother.
units.literal: As the empress was dying, the Empress Dowager asked about her kin; she said that Hongzhi was her brother.

units.zh: 與相訣經日，具條列南方諸兄珍之等，手以付洪之。
units.en: After many days of parting words, she wrote out a full list of her southern brothers, including Zhenzhi, and handed it to Hongzhi.
units.literal: Having taken leave of each other for many days, she fully listed her southern brothers Zhenzhi and the others by hand and delivered it to Hongzhi.

units.zh: 遂號為獻文親舅。
units.en: He was thereafter styled Emperor Xianwen's maternal uncle.
units.literal: He was thereupon styled Emperor Xianwen's maternal uncle.

units.zh: 太安中，珍之等兄弟至都，與洪之相見，敘元後平生故事，計長幼為昆季。
units.en: During the Tai'an era Zhenzhi and his brothers reached the capital. Meeting Hongzhi, they recounted the empress's life and, by order of age, became sworn brothers.
units.literal: In the Tai'an era Zhenzhi and his brothers arrived at the capital; meeting Hongzhi they recounted the empress's life story and, reckoning age order, became fraternal kin.

units.zh: 以外戚為河內太守，進爵任城侯，威儀一同刺史。
units.en: As a maternal relative of the throne he was appointed governor of Henei, advanced to Marquis of Rencheng, and accorded the ceremonial rank of a provincial governor.
units.literal: By virtue of his position as maternal kin he became governor of Henei, was advanced to Marquis of Rencheng, and his pomp equaled that of a provincial governor.

units.zh: 河內北連上党，南接武牢，地險人悍，數為劫害，長吏不能禁。
units.en: Henei bordered Shangdang to the north and Wulao to the south. The terrain was rugged and the people fierce; banditry was frequent and local officials could not suppress it.
units.literal: Henei bordered on Shangdang to the north and Wulao to the south—the terrain perilous, the people fierce; robbery and harm occurred repeatedly and prefectural officials could not restrain them.

units.zh: 洪之至郡，嚴設科防，募斬賊者，便加重賞，勤勸務本，盜賊止息。
units.en: When Hongzhi took office he imposed strict regulations, offered heavy rewards for beheading bandits, and urged the people to return to honest livelihood; banditry ceased.
units.literal: When Hongzhi reached the commandery he strictly established regulations and defenses, recruited those who beheaded brigands with increased rewards at once, and diligently urged devotion to fundamentals—brigandage ceased.

units.zh: 誅鋤奸黨，過為酷虐。
units.en: In rooting out traitorous factions he went beyond all bounds into cruelty.
units.literal: He executed and uprooted traitorous factions, going beyond proper bounds into cruelty.

units.zh: 後為懷州刺史，封漢郡公，徵拜內都大官。
units.en: Later he became governor of Huai Province, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han Commandery, and was summoned as Grand Director of the Inner Court.
units.literal: Later he was governor of Huaizhou, enfeoffed as Duke of Han Commandery, and summoned as Grand Director of the Inner Court.

units.zh: 河西羌胡領部落反叛，獻文親征，命洪之與侍中、東郡王陸定總統諸軍。
units.en: When Qiang and Hu tribal leaders in Hexi rebelled, Emperor Xianwen campaigned in person and ordered Hongzhi and the Attendant Secretary, Prince of Dongjun Lu Ding, to command all the armies.
units.literal: The Qiang and Hu of Hexi leading tribes rebelled; Emperor Xianwen personally campaigned and ordered Hongzhi together with the Attendant Secretary and Prince of Dongjun, Lu Ding, to command all the armies.

units.zh: 輿駕至并州，詔洪之為河西都將，討山胡。
units.en: When the imperial procession reached Bing Province, he appointed Hongzhi General of Hexi to campaign against the mountain Hu.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Bingzhou he appointed Hongzhi commander of Hexi (dujiang) to campaign against the mountain Hu.

units.zh: 皆保險距戰，洪之築壘於石樓南白雞原以對之。
units.en: They all held defensible ground and resisted. Hongzhi built fortifications at Baiji Plain south of Shilou to confront them.
units.literal: All relied on defensible terrain and resisted in battle; Hongzhi built ramparts at Baiji Plain south of Shilou to confront them.

units.zh: 時諸將悉欲進攻，洪之乃開以大信，聽其復業。
units.en: Though all the generals wished to attack, Hongzhi instead offered generous terms and allowed them to resume their livelihoods.
units.literal: At that time all the generals wished to attack; Hongzhi instead opened with great faith and allowed them to resume their livelihoods.

units.zh: 胡人遂降。
units.en: The Hu thereupon surrendered.
units.literal: The Hu people thereupon surrendered.

units.zh: 獻文嘉之。
units.en: Emperor Xianwen commended him.
units.literal: Emperor Xianwen commended this.

units.zh: 遷拜尚書、外都大官。
units.en: He was promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Director of the Outer Court.
units.literal: He was transferred and appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Director of the Outer Court.

units.zh: 後為使持節、安南將軍、秦、益二州刺史。
units.en: Later he served as Commissioner with the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the South, and governor of Qin and Yi provinces.
units.literal: Later he held the post of Commissioner with the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the South, and governor of Qin and Yi provinces.

units.zh: 至任，設禁奸之制。
units.en: On taking office he established regulations to suppress wrongdoing.
units.literal: On assuming office he established regulations for restraining wickedness.

units.zh: 有帶刃行者，罪與劫同。
units.en: Anyone found carrying a blade on the road was punished as for robbery.
units.literal: Whoever walked bearing a blade—his crime was the same as robbery.

units.zh: 輕重品格，各有條章。
units.en: Grades of severity and leniency were each set forth in written articles.
units.literal: Graded standards of severity and leniency each had their articles.

units.zh: 於是大饗州中豪傑長老，示之法制。
units.en: He then held a great feast for the province's leading men and elders and displayed the regulations to them.
units.literal: He then greatly feasted the eminent elders and seniors of the province and showed them the legal system.

units.zh: 乃夜密遣騎分部覆諸要路，有犯禁者，輒捉送州，宣告斬決。
units.en: That night he secretly sent cavalry in detachments to cover the main roads. Anyone who violated the prohibitions was seized, sent to the provincial capital, and publicly beheaded.
units.literal: That night he secretly dispatched riders in sections to cover the vital roads; whoever violated the prohibitions was seized and sent to the province, where he was proclaimed and beheaded.

units.zh: 其中枉見殺害者，至有百數。
units.en: Among those killed, the wrongly executed numbered as many as a hundred.
units.literal: Among them those wrongly killed numbered up to a hundred.

units.zh: 赤葩渴郎羌深居山谷，雖相羈縻，王人罕到。
units.en: The Chipo Kelang Qiang lived deep in mountain valleys. Though nominally under imperial restraint, royal officials seldom reached them.
units.literal: The Chipo Kelang Qiang lived deep in mountain valleys; though nominally restrained, royal officials seldom reached them.

units.zh: 洪之芟山為道，廣十餘步，示以軍行之勢。
units.en: Hongzhi cut a road through the mountains more than ten paces wide, displaying the might of a marching army.
units.literal: Hongzhi cleared mountains to make a road more than ten paces wide, displaying the might of an army on the march.

units.zh: 乃興軍臨其境，山人驚駭。
units.en: He then marched into their territory, and the mountaineers were struck with terror.
units.literal: He then raised troops and advanced to their territory; the mountaineers were alarmed and terrified.

units.zh: 洪之將數十騎至其里閭，撫其妻子，問所疾苦，因資遺之。
units.en: Hongzhi rode with several dozen horsemen to their villages, comforted their wives and children, asked after their hardships, and gave them provisions and gifts.
units.literal: Hongzhi with several tens of riders went to their hamlets, comforted their wives and children, asked what hardships they suffered, and thereby gave them provisions and gifts.

units.zh: 眾羌喜悅，求編課調，所入十倍於常。
units.en: The Qiang were delighted and asked to be enrolled for taxation; revenue came to ten times the usual amount.
units.literal: The Qiang masses were pleased; they asked to be enrolled for tax and levy—the revenue came to ten times the usual amount.

units.zh: 洪之善禦戎夷，頗有威惠，而刻害之聲，聞於朝野。
units.en: Hongzhi was skilled in governing frontier peoples and wielded both authority and grace, yet reports of his cruelty were heard throughout court and countryside.
units.literal: Hongzhi was skilled in controlling barbarian tribes and had considerable authority and grace, yet reports of harsh cruelty were heard throughout court and countryside.

units.zh: 初，洪之微時妻張氏，亦聰強婦人，自貧賤至富貴，多所補益，有男女幾十人。
units.en: In his early days Hongzhi's wife Lady Zhang was herself an intelligent and forceful woman. From poverty to wealth she contributed greatly to his rise, and they had several dozen sons and daughters.
units.literal: Earlier, when Hongzhi was still obscure, his wife Lady Zhang was also an intelligent and forceful woman; from poverty to wealth she contributed much, and they had several tens of sons and daughters.

units.zh: 洪之後得劉芳從姊，重之，疏張氏。
units.en: Later Hongzhi took a cousin of Liu Fang as a second wife, favored her, and grew distant from Lady Zhang.
units.literal: Later Hongzhi obtained a cousin of Liu Fang, favored her highly, and grew distant from Lady Zhang.

units.zh: 亦多所產育。
units.en: She too bore many children.
units.literal: She too bore many children.

units.zh: 為兩宅別居，偏厚劉室，由是二妻妒競，兩宅母子，往來如仇。
units.en: He maintained two separate households, favoring the Liu household disproportionately. The two wives competed in jealousy, and mothers and children of the two houses treated one another as enemies.
units.literal: He maintained two separate households with disproportionate favor to the Liu residence; because of this the two wives competed in jealousy, and mothers and children of the two houses came and went like enemies.

units.zh: 及蒞西州，以劉自隨。
units.en: When he took office in the Western Provinces he brought Lady Liu with him.
units.literal: When he took office in the Western Province he brought Liu with him.

units.zh: 洪之素非廉清，每有受納。
units.en: Hongzhi had never been honest in office and frequently accepted bribes.
units.literal: Hongzhi had never been clean in integrity; he frequently accepted bribes.

units.zh: 時孝文始建祿制，法禁嚴峻，遂鎖洪之赴京，親臨太華，庭集群臣數之。
units.en: When Emperor Xiaowen had just established the salary system and laws were stern, Hongzhi was chained and sent to the capital. The emperor came to Taihua Palace, assembled the ministers in court, and recounted his crimes.
units.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowen had just established the salary system—laws and prohibitions were stern—and so Hongzhi was chained and sent to the capital; the emperor himself came to Taihua, assembled the ministers in the courtyard, and counted his crimes.

units.zh: 以其大臣，聽在家自裁。
units.en: Because he was a senior minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.
units.literal: Because he was a great minister, he was permitted to take his own life at home.

units.zh: 洪之志性慷慨，多所堪忍。
units.en: Hongzhi's disposition was bold and generous; he endured what others could scarcely bear.
units.literal: Hongzhi's disposition was lofty and generous; he bore much that others could scarcely endure.

units.zh: 疹病炙療，艾炷圍將二寸，首足十餘處，一時俱下，言笑自若，接賓不輟。
units.en: When ill he underwent cauterization: the moxa cones were nearly two inches across, applied at more than ten points on head and feet all at once, yet he spoke and laughed as usual and never ceased receiving guests.
units.literal: When ill he sought cauterization treatment; the moxa cones would measure nearly two inches around, more than ten places on head and feet—when all were applied at once he spoke and laughed as usual, receiving guests without cease.

units.zh: 及臨盡，沐浴衣幍，防卒扶持，出入遍巡家庭，如是再三，泣歎良久，乃臥而引藥。
units.en: As death approached he bathed, dressed in mourning garments, and with guards supporting him walked through every room of the house again and again, weeping for a long time before lying down and taking poison.
units.literal: When he was near the end he bathed and donned mourning cap and robe; guards supported him as he went in and out, touring the entire household again and again, weeping and sighing for a long while, then lay down and took poison.

units.zh: 始洪之托為元後兄，公私自同外戚。
units.en: At first Hongzhi had passed himself off as Empress Yuan's brother and was privately treated as a member of the imperial maternal clan.
units.literal: At first Hongzhi had pretended to be the Empress Yuan's brother, and in private was treated like maternal kin.

units.zh: 至此罪後，孝文乃稍對百官辯其誣假。
units.en: Only after his crimes were exposed did Emperor Xiaowen gradually explain to the court that the kinship had been a fraud.
units.literal: Only after this crime did Emperor Xiaowen gradually explain to the officials that the claim was false.

units.zh: 而諸李猶善相視，恩紀如親。
units.en: Yet the Li family still treated one another with affection, their bonds as close as blood kin.
units.literal: Yet the various Lis still treated one another well, their bonds of favor like kin.

units.zh: 洪之始見元後，計年為兄。
units.en: When Hongzhi first met Empress Yuan, he reckoned himself her elder brother by age.
units.literal: When Hongzhi first met the Empress Yuan, he reckoned by age to be her elder brother.

units.zh: 及珍之等至，洪之以元後素定長幼，其呼拜坐，皆如家人。
units.en: When Zhenzhi and his brothers arrived, Hongzhi—relying on the empress's long-established order of seniority—addressed them, bowed, and seated himself exactly as among family.
units.literal: When Zhenzhi and the others arrived, Hongzhi, because the empress had long since fixed senior and junior order, in address, bowing, and seating all acted as a family.

units.zh: 暮年，數延攜之宴飲。
units.en: In his later years he often invited them to feasts.
units.literal: In his later years he frequently invited them to banquets and drinking.

units.zh: 醉酣之後，時或言及本末，洪之則起而加敬，笑語自若。
units.en: When drunk they sometimes spoke of how the relationship had begun; Hongzhi would rise and show added deference, yet laugh and talk as before.
units.literal: After deep drunkenness they sometimes spoke of how it all began; Hongzhi would rise and show added respect, laughing and talking as usual.

units.zh: 富貴赫奕，舅戚之家。
units.en: Their wealth and splendor blazed like a great house of imperial kin.
units.literal: Wealth and honor blazed brilliantly—a house of maternal kin.

units.zh: 遂棄宗，專附珍之等。
units.en: He then abandoned his own clan and attached himself solely to Zhenzhi and his brothers.
units.literal: He thereupon abandoned his own clan and attached himself solely to Zhenzhi and the others.

units.zh: 後頗存振本屬，而猶不顯然。
units.en: Later he made some effort to support his original clan, but only in private.
units.literal: Later he somewhat preserved ties to his original clan, yet still not openly.

units.zh: 劉氏四子。
units.en: Lady Liu bore four sons.
units.literal: The Liu clan had four sons.

units.zh: 子神
units.en: His son Shen
units.literal: His son Shen

units.zh: 長子神，少有膽略，以氣尚為名。
units.en: The eldest son, Shen, was bold and resourceful from youth and was renowned for spirited valor.
units.literal: Shen of Changzi was bold and resourceful from youth and was renowned for spirited valor.

units.zh: 以軍功封長樂縣男，累遷平東將軍、太中大夫。
units.en: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changle County and rose through the ranks to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
units.literal: For military merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changle County and rose in succession to General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

units.zh: 孝昌中，行相州事，尋正加撫軍。
units.en: During the Xiaochang era he acted as governor of Xiang Province and was soon formally appointed General Who Pacifies the Army.
units.literal: In the Xiaochang era he acted as governor of Xiang Province and was soon formally appointed General Who Pacifies the Army.

units.zh: 葛榮盡銳攻之，久不能克。
units.en: Ge Rong attacked him with all his best troops but for a long time could not overcome him.
units.literal: Ge Rong attacked him with all his best troops but for a long time could not overcome him.

units.zh: 會葛榮見禽，以功進爵為公。
units.en: When Ge Rong was captured, he was advanced to duke for his merit.
units.literal: When Ge Rong was captured, he was advanced to duke for his merit.

units.zh: 元顥入洛，莊帝北巡，以神為侍中。
units.en: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and Emperor Xiaozhuang toured north, Shen was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and Emperor Xiaozhuang toured north, Shen was made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 又除殿中尚書，仍行相州事。
units.en: He was also appointed Director of the Palace Department while continuing to act as governor of Xiang Province.
units.literal: He was also appointed Director of the Palace Department while continuing to act as governor of Xiang Province.

units.zh: 車駕還宮，改封安康郡公。
units.en: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, his fief was changed to Duke of Ankang Commandery.
units.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, his fief was changed to Duke of Ankang Commandery.

units.zh: 普泰元年，進驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、相州大中正。
units.en: In the first year of Putai he was promoted to General of Fast Cavalry, Honorably Equivalent to the Three Highest Ministers, and Chief Rectifier of Xiang Province.
units.literal: In the first year of Putai he was promoted to General of Fast Cavalry, Honorably Equivalent to the Three Highest Ministers, and Chief Rectifier of Xiang Province.

units.zh: 薨，贈司徒公，冀州刺史。
units.en: He died and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works and Governor of Ji Province.
units.literal: He died and was posthumously given Minister of Works and Governor of Ji Province.

units.zh: 子士䋤。
units.en: His son was Shi Yao.
units.literal: His son was Shi Yao.

units.zh: 齊受禪，例降。
units.en: When Qi received the transfer of the mandate, his rank was reduced by precedent.
units.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced by precedent.

units.zh: 張赦提
units.en: Zhang Sheti
units.literal: Zhang Sheti

units.zh: 張赦提，中山安喜人也。
units.en: Zhang Sheti was a native of Anxi in Zhongshan.
units.literal: Zhang Sheti was a man of Anxi in Zhongshan.

units.zh: 性雄武，有規畫。
units.en: He was bold and martial by nature and skilled in planning.
units.literal: By nature he was bold and martial, with strategic planning.

units.zh: 初為武卉中郎。
units.en: He first served as a Rapid-as-Tigers Palace Gentleman.
units.literal: At first he was a Central Gentleman of Wuhui.

units.zh: 時京畿盜魁，首稱豹子、彪子，並善弓馬，於靈丘、應門間聚為劫害。
units.en: At that time the leading bandits of the capital region were known as Baozi and Biaozi. Both were skilled horsemen and archers who gathered between Lingqiu and Yanmen to rob and plunder.
units.literal: At that time the chief bandits of the capital region were known foremost as Baozi and Biaozi; both were skilled in bow and horse, and between Lingqiu and Yingmen gathered to plunder and harm.

units.zh: 至乃斬人首，射其口，刺人臍，引腸繞樹而共射之，以為戲笑。
units.en: They would behead victims, shoot arrows into their mouths, stab their navels, draw out their intestines and wrap them around trees for target practice—all as sport.
units.literal: They would even cut off people's heads, shoot their mouths, stab people's navels, draw out the intestines and wrap them around trees to shoot at together, taking it as sport and laughter.

units.zh: 其暴酷如此。
units.en: Their cruelty was beyond measure.
units.literal: Their brutality and cruelty were such as this.

units.zh: 軍騎掩捕，久弗能獲，行者患焉。
units.en: Government cavalry hunted them for a long time without success, and travelers lived in fear.
units.literal: Cavalry made surprise arrests but for a long time could not capture them; travelers were afflicted by this.

units.zh: 赦提為逐賊軍將，未幾而獲彪子、豹子及其黨與，盡送京師，斬於闕下，自是清靜。
units.en: Sheti was appointed general to pursue the bandits. Before long he captured Biaozi, Baozi, and their followers, sent them to the capital, and had them beheaded at the palace gate. The region was thereafter at peace.
units.literal: Sheti became general of the army pursuing bandits; before long he captured Biaozi, Baozi, and their followers, sent them all to the capital, and beheaded them below the palace gate—thereafter all was quiet.

units.zh: 其靈丘羅思祖，宗門豪溢，家處隘險，多止亡命，與之為劫。
units.en: At Lingqiu, Luo Sizu of a powerful clan lived in rugged terrain where many fugitives gathered and joined him in banditry.
units.literal: At Lingqiu, Luo Sizu of a clan overflowing with power had his house in narrow perilous terrain; many fugitives stayed there and joined him in robbery.

units.zh: 獻文怒之，孥戮其家。
units.en: Emperor Xianwen was enraged and executed his entire family.
units.literal: Emperor Xianwen was enraged and exterminated his entire family.

units.zh: 而思祖家黨，相率寇盜。
units.en: Yet Sizu's clansmen and followers turned to banditry in succession.
units.literal: Yet Sizu's clan and partisans one after another turned to raiding and robbery.

units.zh: 赦提募求捕逐。
units.en: Sheti recruited men to hunt them down.
units.literal: Sheti recruited men to seek and capture them.

units.zh: 以赦提為遊徼軍將，前後擒獲，殺之略盡。
units.en: Appointed patrol general, Sheti captured and killed nearly all of them.
units.literal: Sheti was made general of patrol forces; in successive captures he killed nearly all of them.

units.zh: 因此，濫有屠害，尤為忍酷。
units.en: In the process he slaughtered indiscriminately, showing exceptional cruelty.
units.literal: Because of this there was indiscriminate slaughter; he was especially cruel and pitiless.

units.zh: 既資前稱，又藉此功，除幽州刺史，假安喜侯。
units.en: On the strength of his earlier reputation and this achievement, he was appointed governor of You Province with acting rank as Marquis of Anxi.
units.literal: Relying on his earlier reputation and also on this merit, he was appointed governor of Youzhou with acting rank as Marquis of Anxi.

units.zh: 赦提克己厲約，遂有清稱。
units.en: Sheti disciplined himself and enforced austerity, earning a reputation for integrity.
units.literal: Sheti restrained himself and enforced frugality, and thereupon gained a reputation for integrity.

units.zh: 後頗縱妻段氏，多有受納。
units.en: Later he indulged his wife Lady Duan, and many bribes were accepted.
units.literal: Later he rather indulged his wife Lady Duan, and there were many bribes accepted.

units.zh: 命僧尼因事通請，貪虐流聞。
units.en: He used monks and nuns to solicit favors on his behalf, and reports of his greed and cruelty spread widely.
units.literal: He ordered monks and nuns to petition on various matters; reports of greed and cruelty spread.

units.zh: 中散李真香出使幽州，採訪牧守政績。
units.en: Palace Attendant Li Zhenxiang was sent to You Province to investigate the conduct of regional governors.
units.literal: Li Zhenxiang, a Palace Attendant, went on mission to Youzhou to investigate the achievements of regional governors.

units.zh: 真香驗案其罪，赦提懼死欲逃。
units.en: Zhenxiang verified his crimes, and Sheti, fearing execution, planned to flee.
units.literal: Zhenxiang verified and prosecuted his crimes; Sheti feared death and wished to flee.

units.zh: 其妻姑為太尉、東陽王丕妻，恃丕親貴，自許詣丕申訴求助，謂赦提曰：「當為訴理，幸得申雪，願寬憂，不為異計。」
units.en: His wife's aunt was the wife of Grand Marshal Prince of Dongyang Pi. Relying on Pi's influence, she promised to appeal to him and told Sheti, "I will plead your case. With luck you will be cleared—set your mind at ease and make no rash move."
units.literal: His wife's aunt was wife to the Grand Marshal, Prince of Dongyang Pi; relying on Pi's kinship and nobility, she promised to go to Pi to plead for help, telling Sheti: "I shall plead your case; with luck you will be cleared—set your mind at ease and make no other plans."

units.zh: 赦提以此，差自解慰。
units.en: Sheti was somewhat reassured by this.
units.literal: Because of this Sheti was somewhat relieved and comforted.

units.zh: 段乃陳列：真香昔嘗因假而過幽州，知赦提有好牛，從索不果。
units.en: Lady Duan then argued that Zhenxiang had once passed through You Province on leave, learned that Sheti owned a fine ox, and failed to obtain it when he asked.
units.literal: Lady Duan then set forth: Zhenxiang had once passed through Youzhou on leave and, knowing Sheti had a fine ox, sought it from him without success.

units.zh: 令台使止挾前事，故威逼部下，拷楚過極，橫以無辜，證成誣罪。
units.en: Bearing this grudge, she claimed, he had coerced Sheti's subordinates with excessive torture and fabricated crimes against the innocent.
units.literal: She had the imperial envoy seize on that prior matter; therefore he coerced subordinates by intimidation, tortured beyond all bounds, and on the innocent fabricated false guilt.

units.zh: 執事恐有不盡，使駕部令趙秦州重往究訊，事狀如前，處赦提大辟。
units.en: The authorities, fearing the investigation was incomplete, sent Director of the Imperial Carriage Zhao Qinzhou to reinvestigate. The facts were confirmed as before, and Sheti was sentenced to death.
units.literal: The authorities, fearing the matter was not fully settled, sent Director of the Imperial Carriage Zhao Qinzhou to reinvestigate; the facts were as before, and Sheti was sentenced to the death penalty.

units.zh: 孝文詔賜死於第。
units.en: Emperor Xiaowen ordered that he be permitted to die at his residence.
units.literal: Emperor Xiaowen ordered that he be granted death at his residence.

units.zh: 將就盡，命妻而責之曰：「貪濁穢吾者卿也，又安吾而不得免禍，九泉之下，當為仇仇矣。」
units.en: As death approached he summoned his wife and reproached her: "You are the one who stained me with greed, reassured me yet could not save me from ruin. In the grave we shall be mortal enemies."
units.literal: As he was about to die he summoned his wife and reproached her: "It was you who stained me with greed and corruption, and who reassured me yet could not spare me from disaster—in the nine springs below we shall be mortal enemies."

units.zh: 又有華山太守趙霸，酷暴非理。
units.en: There was also Zhao Ba, governor of Huashan, whose cruelty and violence knew no bounds.
units.literal: There was also Zhao Ba, governor of Huashan, cruel and violent beyond reason.

units.zh: 大使崔光奏霸云：「不遵憲度，威虐任情，至乃手擊吏人，僚屬奔走，不可以君人字下，納之軌物。
units.en: Commissioner Cui Guang memorialized against Ba: "He disregards the laws, rules through arbitrary cruelty, and even strikes officials with his own hands until his subordinates flee in terror. He cannot be allowed to govern the people or bring order to the realm.
units.literal: Commissioner Cui Guang memorialized against Ba, saying: "He does not observe the laws and statutes, acts with arbitrary intimidation and cruelty, even to the point of striking officials with his own hands so that subordinates flee in terror—he cannot be allowed to rule over the people and bring them within the norms.

units.zh: 輒禁止在州。」
units.en: He should be detained in the province at once."
units.literal: He should forthwith be detained in the province."

units.zh: 詔免所居官。
units.en: An edict removed him from office.
units.literal: An edict removed him from his post.

units.zh: 崔暹，字元欽，本雲清河東武城人也，世家於滎陽、潁川之間。
units.en: Cui Xuan, courtesy name Yuanqin, was said to be from Dongwucheng in Qinghe. His family had long been established between Xingyang and Yingchuan.
units.literal: Cui Xuan, style name Yuanqin, was originally said to be from Dongwucheng in Qinghe; his family had long been established between Xingyang and Yingchuan.

units.zh: 性猛酷，少仁恕，奸猾好利，能事勢家。
units.en: He was fierce and cruel by nature, lacking in mercy, crafty and greedy, and skilled at currying favor with the powerful.
units.literal: By nature he was fierce and cruel, lacking in humanity and forbearance, crafty and greedy, skilled at serving powerful families.

units.zh: 初以秀才累遷南袞州刺史，盜用官瓦，贓汙狼籍，為御史中尉李平所糾，免官。
units.en: Entering office through the xiucai examination, he rose to governor of Southern Yan Province. He misappropriated official tiles, and his corruption was notorious. Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him and he was dismissed.
units.literal: At first through the xiucai examination he rose in succession to governor of Southern Yanzhou; he misappropriated official tiles, and his corruption was in disarray—he was impeached by the Censor-in-Chief Li Ping and dismissed.

units.zh: 後行豫州事，尋即真。
units.en: Later he administered Yu Province and soon received the full appointment.
units.literal: Later he acted as administrator of Yuzhou affairs and soon received the full appointment.

units.zh: 遣子析戶，分隸三縣，廣占田宅，藏匿官奴，障吝陂葦，侵盜公私，為御史中尉王顯所彈，免官。
units.en: He had his son divide the household and register members under three counties, seized extensive lands and properties, concealed government slaves, monopolized pond reeds, and encroached on public and private property. Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian impeached him and he was again dismissed.
units.literal: He sent his son to divide the household and register members under three counties, broadly seized fields and houses, concealed government slaves, obstructed and hoarded pond reeds, and encroached on public and private property—he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Wang Xian and dismissed.

units.zh: 後累遷瀛州刺史。
units.en: Later he rose to governor of Ying Province.
units.literal: Later he rose in succession to governor of Yingzhou.

units.zh: 貪暴安忍，人庶患之。
units.en: Greedy, brutal, and pitiless, he was hated by the people.
units.literal: Greedy, violent, and calmly cruel, the people suffered from him.

units.zh: 嘗出獵州北，單騎至人村，有汲水婦人，暹令飲馬，因問曰：「崔瀛州何如？」
units.en: Once while hunting north of the province he rode alone to a village. A woman was drawing water; Xuan had her water his horse and asked, "How is Governor Cui of Ying Province?"
units.literal: Once when hunting north of the province he rode alone to a village; there was a woman drawing water—Xuan had her water his horse and then asked: "How is Governor Cui of Yingzhou?"

units.zh: 婦人不知是暹，答曰：「百姓何罪！
units.en: Not knowing it was Xuan himself, the woman replied, "What crime have the people committed
units.literal: The woman did not know it was Xuan and answered: "What crime have the common people committed

units.zh: 得如此癩兒刺史。」
units.en: to deserve such a leprous wretch of a governor?"
units.literal: to deserve such a leprous wretch of a governor?"

units.zh: 暹默然而去。
units.en: Xuan departed in silence.
units.literal: Xuan departed in silence.

units.zh: 以不稱職，被解還京。
units.en: Deemed unfit for office, he was dismissed and recalled to the capital.
units.literal: For incompetence he was dismissed and returned to the capital.

units.zh: 武川鎮反，詔暹為都督，李崇討之。
units.en: When Wuchuan Garrison rebelled, Xuan was appointed commander to campaign under Li Chong.
units.literal: When Wuchuan garrison rebelled, an edict appointed Xuan as commander; Li Chong campaigned against them.

units.zh: 違崇節度，為賊所敗，單騎潛還。
units.en: He disobeyed Chong's orders, was defeated by the rebels, and fled back alone.
units.literal: He violated Chong's command, was defeated by the rebels, and returned alone in secret flight.

units.zh: 禁於廷尉，以女妓園田貨元叉獲免。
units.en: He was imprisoned by the Minister of Justice but secured release by bribing Yuan Cha with female entertainers, gardens, and fields.
units.literal: He was imprisoned by the Minister of Justice; with female entertainers, gardens, and fields he bribed Yuan Cha and obtained release.

units.zh: 建義初，遇害於河陰。
units.en: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was killed at Heyin.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he met violent death at Heyin.

units.zh: 贈司徒公、冀州刺史，追封武津縣公。
units.en: He was posthumously honored as Grand Steward and governor of Ji Province, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.
units.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Steward and governor of Jizhou, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wujin County.

units.zh: 子瓚，字祖珍，位兼尚書左丞，卒。
units.en: His son Zan, courtesy name Zuzhen, served as Concurrent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and died in office.
units.literal: His son Zan, style name Zuzhen, held the post of Concurrent Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing and died in office.

units.zh: 瓚妻，莊帝姊也，後封襄城長公主，故特贈瓚冀州刺史。
units.en: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang and was later enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Xiangcheng; Zan was therefore posthumously granted the governorship of Ji Province.
units.literal: Zan's wife was a sister of Emperor Zhuang; later she was enfeoffed as Grand Princess of Xiangcheng, and therefore Zan was specially granted posthumous appointment as governor of Jizhou.

units.zh: 子茂，字祖昂，襲祖爵。
units.en: His son Mao, courtesy name Zu'ang, inherited his grandfather's noble rank.
units.literal: His son Mao, style name Zu'ang, inherited his grandfather's noble rank.

units.zh: 邸珍，字安寶，本中山上曲陽人也，魏太和中，徙居武州鎮。
units.en: Di Zhen, courtesy name Anbao, was originally from Shangquyang in Zhongshan. During the Wei Taihe era his family moved to Wuzhou Garrison.
units.literal: Di Zhen, style name Anbao, was originally from Shangquyang in Zhongshan; in the Taihe era of Wei he moved to Wuzhou garrison.

units.zh: 孝昌中，六鎮兵起，珍遂從杜洛周賊。
units.en: During the Xiaochang era, when the Six Garrisons rebelled, Zhen joined the rebel Du Luozhou.
units.literal: In the Xiaochang era the Six Garrisons rose in arms; Zhen thereupon followed the rebel Du Luozhou.

units.zh: 洛周為葛榮所吞，珍入榮軍。
units.en: When Luozhou was absorbed by Ge Rong, Zhen entered Ge Rong's army.
units.literal: Luozhou was swallowed up by Ge Rong, and Zhen entered Rong's army.

units.zh: 榮為爾硃榮所破，珍與其餘黨，俱徙并州。
units.en: When Ge Rong was defeated by Erzhu Rong, Zhen and the remaining rebels were relocated to Bing Province.
units.literal: Rong was defeated by Erzhu Rong; Zhen and the remaining partisans were all moved to Bingzhou.

units.zh: 從齊神武出山東。
units.en: He followed Northern Qi's Shenwu in his campaign east of the mountains.
units.literal: He followed Qi Shenwu in emerging to Shandong.

units.zh: 神武起義信都，拜珍長史，封上曲縣侯，除殷州刺史。
units.en: When Shenwu raised his army at Xindu he appointed Zhen chief clerk, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangqu County, and made him governor of Yin Province.
units.literal: When Shenwu raised the righteous army at Xindu he appointed Zhen Chief Clerk, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Shangqu County, and made him governor of Yinzhou.

units.zh: 珍求取無厭，大為州人所疾苦。
units.en: Zhen's greed was insatiable, and the people of the province suffered greatly.
units.literal: Zhen's demands were insatiable, and the people of the province suffered greatly from him.

units.zh: 後兼尚書右僕射、大行台，節度諸軍事，擊梁州將成景攜等，解東行圍，回軍彭城。
units.en: Later he served concurrently as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner, directing military affairs. He attacked Liang generals including Cheng Jingxie, lifted the siege of Dongxing, and returned to Pengcheng.
units.literal: Later he concurrently served as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Grand Commissioner, directing all military affairs; he attacked Liang generals Cheng Jingxie and others, lifted the siege of Dongxing, and returned the army to Pengcheng.

units.zh: 珍禦下殘酷，士眾離心，至於土人豪族，遇之無禮，遂為州人所害。
units.en: Zhen ruled his subordinates with cruelty, alienating soldiers and civilians alike, and treated local gentry without courtesy. He was eventually killed by men of the province.
units.literal: Zhen was cruel in governing subordinates; soldiers and masses lost heart; as for local gentry and powerful clans, he treated them without propriety—therefore he was killed by men of the province.

units.zh: 後贈定州刺史、司空公。
units.en: He was later posthumously honored as governor of Ding Province and Minister of Works.
units.literal: Later he was posthumously granted governor of Dingzhou and Minister of Works.

units.zh: 田式，字顯標，馮翊下邽人也。
units.en: Tian Shi, courtesy name Xianbiao, was a native of Xiagui in Fengyi.
units.literal: Tian Shi, style name Xianbiao, was a man of Xiagui in Fengyi.

units.zh: 祖安興、父長樂，仕魏，俱為本郡太守。
units.en: His grandfather Anxing and father Changle both served Wei as governors of their native commandery.
units.literal: His grandfather Anxing and father Changle served Wei; both were governors of their native commandery.

units.zh: 式性剛果，多武藝，拳勇絕人。
units.en: Shi was firm and resolute by nature, skilled in martial arts, and unmatched in physical courage.
units.literal: Shi by nature was firm and resolute, skilled in many martial arts, his fist-fighting courage surpassing others.

units.zh: 仕周，位渭南太守，政尚嚴猛，吏人重足而立，無敢違法。
units.en: Serving the Zhou, he became governor of Weinan. His administration was harsh and severe; officials and commoners alike stood in fear, and none dared break the law.
units.literal: Serving Zhou, he held the post of governor of Weinan; his government favored severity and fierceness—officials and people stood as if on tiptoes, none daring to violate the law.

units.zh: 遷本郡太守，親故屏跡，請托不行。
units.en: Transferred to governor of his native commandery, he kept kin and friends at a distance and accepted no private petitions.
units.literal: He was transferred to governor of his native commandery; kin and friends kept out of sight, and petitions for favor went nowhere.

units.zh: 周武帝聞而善之，進位儀同三司，賜爵信都縣公，擢拜延州刺史。
units.en: Emperor Wu of Zhou heard of this and commended him, promoting him to Equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffing him as Duke of Xindu County, and appointing him governor of Yan Province.
units.literal: Emperor Wu of Zhou heard and approved; he advanced him to Equal to the Three Excellencies, granted him the noble rank of Duke of Xindu County, and promoted him to governor of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 從平齊，以功授上開府，徙為建州刺史，改封梁泉縣公。
units.en: For his service in the conquest of Qi he was granted Superior Opening of the Palace, appointed governor of Jian Province, and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Liangquan County.
units.literal: Following the pacification of Qi, for merit he was granted Superior Opening of the Palace, transferred to governor of Jianzhou, and his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Liangquan County.

units.zh: 後從韋孝寬討尉遲迥，以功拜大將軍，進爵武山郡公。
units.en: Later he followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yuchi Jiong and was appointed Grand General, advanced to Duke of Wushan Commandery.
units.literal: Later he followed Wei Xiaokuan in campaigning against Yuchi Jiong; for merit he was appointed Grand General and advanced to Duke of Wushan Commandery.

units.zh: 及隋文帝受禪，拜襄州總管。
units.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, Shi was appointed regional commander of Xiang Province.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.

units.zh: 專以立威為務，每視事於外，必盛氣以待之。
units.en: He devoted himself solely to inspiring fear. Whenever he held court outside, he awaited his subordinates with fierce intimidation.
units.literal: He devoted himself solely to establishing awe; whenever he conducted affairs outside he always awaited them with fierce bearing.

units.zh: 其下官屬，股栗無敢仰視。
units.en: His subordinates trembled with fear and dared not meet his gaze.
units.literal: His subordinate officials trembled in their thighs and dared not look up.

units.zh: 有犯禁者，雖至親昵，無所容貸。
units.en: Whoever violated his prohibitions, even the closest kin, received no mercy.
units.literal: Whoever violated prohibitions, even the most intimate kin, received no leniency.

units.zh: 其女婿京兆杜甯自長安省之，式誡寧無出外。
units.en: His son-in-law Du Ning of Jingzhao came from Chang'an to visit. Shi forbade him to go outside.
units.literal: His son-in-law Du Ning of Jingzhao came from Chang'an to visit; Shi warned Ning not to go outside.

units.zh: 寧久之不得還，竊上北樓，以暢羈思。
units.en: Unable to return home for a long time, Ning secretly climbed the north tower to ease his longing.
units.literal: Ning for a long time could not return; he secretly went up the north tower to ease his thoughts of being detained.

units.zh: 式知之，杖寧五十。
units.en: When Shi learned of this he had Ning flogged fifty strokes.
units.literal: Shi learned of it and flogged Ning fifty strokes.

units.zh: 其所愛奴，嘗詣式白事，有蟲上其衣衿，揮袖拂去之，式以為慢己，立棒殺之。
units.en: A favorite slave once came to report a matter. When an insect climbed on his collar and the slave brushed it away, Shi took this as disrespect and had him beaten to death on the spot.
units.literal: A favorite slave of his once came to Shi to report a matter; an insect climbed on his collar and he waved his sleeve to brush it away—Shi thought this showed disrespect toward himself and immediately clubbed him to death.

units.zh: 或僚吏奸贓，部內劫盜者，無問輕重，悉禁地阱中，寢處糞穢，令受苦毒。
units.en: Whether corrupt officials or bandits within his jurisdiction, regardless of the severity of the crime, he confined them in underground pits amid filth and excrement to suffer torment.
units.literal: Whether subordinate officials guilty of corruption or bandits and robbers within the district, regardless of severity, all were confined in underground pits, sleeping amid filth and excrement, made to suffer torment.

units.zh: 自非身死，終不得出。
units.en: None were released except by death.
units.literal: Unless they died in body they could never emerge.

units.zh: 每赦書到州，式未暇省讀，先召獄卒殺重囚，然後宣示百姓。
units.en: Whenever an amnesty edict arrived, Shi would not even read it before ordering the execution of serious criminals, and only then proclaim the amnesty to the people.
units.literal: Whenever an amnesty edict reached the province, Shi had no leisure to read it through—he first summoned prison guards to kill the serious criminals, and only then proclaimed it to the people.

units.zh: 其刻暴如此。
units.en: Such was his cruelty.
units.literal: His harsh cruelty was such as this.

units.zh: 由是為上所譴，除名。
units.en: For this the emperor rebuked him and struck his name from the rolls.
units.literal: Because of this he was rebuked by the emperor and struck from the rolls.

units.zh: 式慚恚不食，妻子至其所輒怒，唯侍僮二人，給使左右。
units.en: Ashamed and enraged, Shi refused to eat. When his wife and children approached he grew angry; only two attendant youths remained at his side.
units.literal: Shi, ashamed and enraged, would not eat; when wife and children came to him he grew angry—only two attendant youths served at his side.

units.zh: 從家中索椒，欲自殺，家人不與。
units.en: He demanded pepper from the household with which to kill himself, but his family refused.
units.literal: He demanded pepper from the household to kill himself; the family would not give it.

units.zh: 陰遣侍僮詣市買毒藥，妻子又奪棄之。
units.en: He secretly sent his attendants to buy poison at the market, but his wife seized and discarded it.
units.literal: He secretly sent attendant youths to the market to buy poison; wife and children again seized and discarded it.

units.zh: 式恚臥，其子信時為儀同，至式前流涕曰：「大人既是朝廷重臣，又無大過，比見公卿放辱者多矣，旋復外用，大人何能久乎？
units.en: Lying ill with rage, Shi was visited by his son Xin, then Equal to the Three Excellencies, who wept and said, "Father, you are a senior minister of the court and have committed no grave fault. Many nobles have been dismissed and humiliated only to return to office shortly thereafter. How can you remain in such despair?
units.literal: Shi lay ill with rage; his son Xin, then Equal to the Three Excellencies, came before Shi weeping and said: "Father, you are already a great minister of the court and have committed no great fault—lately one sees many nobles dismissed and humiliated who soon return to external appointment; how can you remain thus for long?

units.zh: 乃至於此！」
units.en: How have you come to this!"
units.literal: Yet you have come to this!"

units.zh: 式欻起抽刀斫信，信避之，刃中於門。
units.en: Shi suddenly rose, drew his sword, and struck at Xin. Xin dodged, and the blade struck the door.
units.literal: Shi suddenly rose, drew his sword, and hacked at Xin; Xin dodged, and the blade struck the door.

units.zh: 上知之，以式為罪己之深，復其官爵，尋拜廣州總管，卒官。
units.en: The emperor learned of this and, moved by Shi's deep self-reproach, restored his rank and office. He was soon appointed regional commander of Guang Province and died in office.
units.literal: The emperor learned of this and, considering how deeply Shi blamed himself, restored his office and noble rank; soon he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Guangzhou and died in office.

units.zh: 燕榮，字貴公，華陰弘農人也。
units.en: Yan Rong, courtesy name Guigong, was a native of Hongnong in Huayin.
units.literal: Yan Rong, style name Guigong, was a man of Hongnong in Huayin.

units.zh: 父侃，周大將軍榮性剛嚴，有武藝。
units.en: His father Kan was a grand general of Zhou. Rong was fierce and strict by nature and skilled in martial arts.
units.literal: His father Kan was a Grand General of Zhou. Rong's nature was fierce and strict, and he was skilled in martial arts.

units.zh: 仕周，為內侍上士。
units.en: He served the Zhou as a senior gentleman of the inner attendants.
units.literal: Serving Zhou, he was a Senior Gentleman of the Inner Attendants.

units.zh: 從武帝伐齊，以功授開府儀同三司，封高邑縣公。
units.en: He followed Emperor Wu in the campaign against Qi and was granted the rank of Opening of the Palace with Ritual Equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyi County.
units.literal: Following Emperor Wu in the campaign against Qi, for merit he was granted Opening of the Palace with Ritual Equal to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyi County.

units.zh: 隋文帝受禪，進位大將軍，進封落叢郡公，拜晉州刺史。
units.en: When Emperor Wen of Sui ascended the throne, Rong was promoted to Grand General and Duke of Luocong Commandery and appointed governor of Jin Province.
units.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication he was advanced to Grand General, promoted to Duke of Luocong Commandery, and appointed governor of Jinzhou.

units.zh: 尋從河間王弘擊突厥，以功拜上柱國，遷青州總管。
units.en: He soon followed Prince of Hejian Hong against the Turks and was appointed Pillar of the State, then regional commander of Qing Province.
units.literal: Soon he followed Prince of Hejian Hong in attacking the Turks; for merit he was appointed Pillar of the State and transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Qingzhou.

units.zh: 在州，選絕有力者為伍伯。
units.en: In the province he selected the strongest men as patrol chiefs.
units.literal: In the province he selected men of exceptional strength as patrol chiefs.

units.zh: 吏人過之者，必加詰問，輒楚撻之，創多見骨。
units.en: Anyone who passed them was interrogated and flogged until the wounds often exposed bone.
units.literal: Officials and people who passed them were always interrogated and forthwith flogged with the cudgel—the wounds often exposed bone.

units.zh: 奸盜屏跡，境內肅然。
units.en: Bandits disappeared and the province grew orderly.
units.literal: Traitors and robbers vanished from sight; within the borders all was solemn and orderly.

units.zh: 他州縣人經其界者，畏若寇仇，不敢休息。
units.en: Travelers from other districts who passed through his territory feared him as they would bandits and dared not pause to rest.
units.literal: People from other prefectures and counties who passed through his territory feared him as bandit enemies and dared not rest.

units.zh: 後因入朝覲，特加恩遇。
units.en: Later, when he came to court for audience, he received special imperial favor.
units.literal: Later when he came to court for audience he received special favor.

units.zh: 榮以母老，請每歲入朝，上許之。
units.en: Because his mother was elderly, Rong requested permission to attend court annually, and the emperor granted it.
units.literal: Rong, because his mother was old, requested to come to court every year; the emperor granted it.

units.zh: 伐陳之役，以為行軍總管，率水軍自東萊傍海入太湖，取吳郡。
units.en: During the campaign against Chen he served as campaigning commander, leading naval forces from Donglai along the coast into Taihu Lake and capturing Wu Commandery.
units.literal: In the campaign against Chen he was made campaigning commander-in-chief, leading the naval forces from Donglai along the sea into Taihu Lake and taking Wu Commandery.

units.zh: 既破丹陽，吳人共立蕭瓛，為宇文述所敗，退保包山。
units.en: After Danyang fell, the Wu people set up Xiao Kan as leader. Defeated by Yuwen Shu, Kan retreated to Baoshan.
units.literal: After Danyang was broken, the Wu people together set up Xiao Kan; he was defeated by Yuwen Shu and retreated to hold Baoshan.

units.zh: 榮率精甲躡之，瓛敗走，為榮所執。
units.en: Rong pursued with elite troops. Kan was defeated, fled, and was captured.
units.literal: Rong led elite armor in pursuit; Kan was defeated and fled and was captured by Rong.

units.zh: 事平，檢校揚州總管。
units.en: When the campaign ended he was appointed acting regional commander of Yang Province.
units.literal: When the affair was settled he was made acting Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou.

units.zh: 尋徵為武候將軍，後除幽州總管。
units.en: He was soon summoned as General of the Martial Guard and later appointed regional commander of You Province.
units.literal: Soon he was summoned as General of the Martial Guard; later he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou.

units.zh: 榮性嚴酷，有威容，長吏見者，莫不惶懼自失。
units.en: Rong was severe and cruel by nature, with an intimidating presence. Senior officials who met him were struck with terror.
units.literal: Rong's nature was severe and cruel; he had an awe-inspiring bearing—senior officials who saw him all lost themselves in fear and dread.

units.zh: 范陽盧氏，世為著姓，榮皆署為吏卒，以屈辱之。
units.en: The Lu clan of Fanyang was an eminent family for generations. Rong appointed them all as clerks and runners to humiliate them.
units.literal: The Lu clan of Fanyang had for generations been a prominent surname; Rong appointed them all as clerks and runners to humiliate them.

units.zh: 鞭笞左右，動至千數，流血盈前，飲啖自若。
units.en: He flogged his attendants by the thousand until blood pooled before him, yet ate and drank as usual.
units.literal: He flogged those at his side, the strokes often reaching a thousand; blood filled the space before him, yet he ate and drank as usual.

units.zh: 嘗按部，道次見叢荊，堪為笞箠，命取之，輒以試人。
units.en: Once on tour he saw brambles suitable for whips along the road, ordered them cut, and used them to test his punishments on people.
units.literal: Once on an inspection tour he saw a thicket of brambles along the road suitable for rods and whips; he ordered them taken and forthwith used them to test people.

units.zh: 人或自陳無咎，榮曰：'後有罪，當免。」
units.en: When someone protested his innocence, Rong said, "If you commit a crime later, you shall be pardoned."
units.literal: When someone declared himself innocent, Rong said: "If you commit a crime later, you shall be pardoned."

units.zh: 及後犯細過，將撾之，人曰：「前日被杖，許有罪宥之。」
units.en: When the man later committed a minor offense and was about to be beaten, he said, "When you flogged me before, you promised to pardon any future offense."
units.literal: When later he committed a minor fault and was about to be beaten, the man said: "The other day when I was flogged you promised that if I had a crime you would pardon it."

units.zh: 榮曰：「無過尚爾，況有過邪！」
units.en: Rong replied, "When you were innocent I still beat you—how much more now that you are guilty!"
units.literal: Rong said: "When you had no fault it was still thus—how much more when you have a fault!"

units.zh: 榜捶如舊。
units.en: He beat him as before.
units.literal: He beat him as before.

units.zh: 榮每巡省管內，聞人吏妻有美色，輒舍其室而淫之，貪暴放縱日甚。
units.en: On his tours, whenever he heard that an official's wife was beautiful, he would enter their home and violate her. His greed, violence, and license grew worse daily.
units.literal: Whenever Rong toured and inspected within his jurisdiction, hearing that an official's wife was beautiful he would enter their house and violate her; his greed, violence, and license grew daily worse.

units.zh: 時元弘嗣除幽州長史，懼辱，固辭。
units.en: When Yuan Hongsi was appointed chief clerk of You Province, he firmly declined, fearing humiliation.
units.literal: At that time Yuan Hongsi was appointed Chief Clerk of Youzhou; fearing humiliation, he firmly declined.

units.zh: 上知之，敕榮曰：「弘嗣杖十已上罪，皆奏聞。」
units.en: The emperor learned of this and ordered Rong, "For Hongsi, all punishments of ten strokes or more must be reported to the throne."
units.literal: The emperor learned of this and ordered Rong: "For Hongsi, all crimes warranting ten strokes or more must be reported to the throne."

units.zh: 榮忿曰：「豎子何敢弄我！」
units.en: Rong raged, "How dare that stripling make a fool of me!"
units.literal: Rong said in anger: "How dare that stripling toy with me!"

units.zh: 及遣弘嗣監納倉粟，颺得一糠一秕，罰之，每笞不滿十，然一日中或至三數。
units.en: When he sent Hongsi to supervise grain collection, he punished him for every husk or chaff found—each beating fewer than ten strokes, yet two or three times a day.
units.literal: When he sent Hongsi to supervise the receipt of granary grain, if a single husk or chaff was winnowed out he punished him—each flogging fewer than ten strokes, yet in one day there might be two or three rounds.

units.zh: 如是歷年，怨隙日構。
units.en: For years their enmity deepened.
units.literal: Thus for years their enmity grew daily.

units.zh: 榮遂收付獄，禁絕其糧。
units.en: Rong had him imprisoned and cut off his food.
units.literal: Rong thereupon had him arrested and imprisoned, cutting off his food.

units.zh: 弘嗣饑，抽衣絮雜水咽之。
units.en: Starving, Hongsi pulled stuffing from his clothes, mixed it with water, and swallowed it.
units.literal: Hongsi, starving, pulled stuffing from his clothes, mixed it with water, and swallowed it.

units.zh: 其妻詣闕稱冤，上遣考功侍郎劉士龍馳驛鞫問，奏榮毒虐，又贓穢狼籍，遂征還京，賜死。
units.en: His wife appealed at the palace gate. The emperor sent Vice Director of Merit Evaluation Liu Shilong to investigate. Liu reported Rong's cruelty and corruption. Rong was recalled to the capital and ordered to take his own life.
units.literal: His wife went to the palace gate to proclaim injustice; the emperor sent Vice Director of Merit Evaluation Liu Shilong by post-chaise to investigate; he memorialized that Rong was poisonous and cruel and also corrupt in disarray—Rong was summoned back to the capital and granted death.

units.zh: 先是，榮家寢室無故有蛆數斛從地墳出。
units.en: Earlier, several bushels of maggots had suddenly emerged from the ground in Rong's bedchamber.
units.literal: Earlier, in Rong's family sleeping chamber, for no reason several hu of maggots suddenly emerged from the ground.

units.zh: 未幾，榮死於蛆出之處。
units.en: Before long Rong died in that very place.
units.literal: Before long Rong died at the place where the maggots had emerged.

units.zh: 有子詢。
units.en: He had a son named Xun.
units.literal: He had a son Xun.

units.zh: 元弘嗣
units.en: Yuan Hongsi
units.literal: Yuan Hongsi

units.zh: 元弘嗣，河南洛陽人也。
units.en: Yuan Hongsi was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
units.literal: Yuan Hongsi was a man of Luoyang in Henan.

units.zh: 祖剛，魏漁陽王。
units.en: His grandfather Gang was Prince of Yuyang under the Wei.
units.literal: His grandfather Gang was Prince of Yuyang under Wei.

units.zh: 父經，周漁陽郡公。
units.en: His father Jing was Duke of Yuyang Commandery under the Zhou.
units.literal: His father Jing was Duke of Yuyang Commandery under Zhou.

units.zh: 弘嗣少襲爵，十八為左親衛。
units.en: Hongsi inherited his noble rank in youth and at eighteen became a Left Imperial Guard.
units.literal: Hongsi in youth inherited the noble rank; at eighteen he was a Left Imperial Guard.

units.zh: 開皇元年，從晉王平陳，以功授上儀同。
units.en: In the first year of Kaihuang he followed the Prince of Jin in the conquest of Chen and was granted Superior Palace Attendant of the Same Rank.
units.literal: In the first year of Kaihuang he followed the Prince of Jin in pacifying Chen and for merit was granted Superior Palace Attendant of the Same Rank.

units.zh: 後除觀州長史，以嚴峻任事，州人多怨之。
units.en: Later he was appointed chief clerk of Guan Province. His stern severity made him widely resented.
units.literal: Later he was appointed Chief Clerk of Guanzhou; for stern severity in office the people of the province mostly resented him.

units.zh: 轉幽州。
units.en: He was transferred to You Province.
units.literal: He was transferred to Youzhou.

units.zh: 時總管燕榮肆虐於弘嗣，每笞辱。
units.en: The regional commander Yan Rong constantly flogged and humiliated him.
units.literal: At that time the Commander-in-Chief Yan Rong vented his tyranny on Hongsi, flogging and humiliating him constantly.

units.zh: 弘嗣心不伏，遂被禁。
units.en: Hongsi refused to submit and was imprisoned.
units.literal: Hongsi's heart would not submit; he was thereupon imprisoned.

units.zh: 及榮誅，弘嗣為政，酷又甚之。
units.en: After Rong was executed, Hongsi took power—and his cruelty exceeded Rong's.
units.literal: When Rong was executed, Hongsi took power—his cruelty was even greater.

units.zh: 每鞫囚，多以酢灌鼻，或椓弋其下竅。
units.en: When interrogating prisoners he often poured vinegar into their nostrils or drove stakes into their lower bodies.
units.literal: Whenever he interrogated prisoners he often poured vinegar into their nostrils or drove stakes into their lower orifices.

units.zh: 無敢隱情，奸偽屏息。
units.en: None dared conceal the truth, and fraud ceased.
units.literal: None dared conceal the truth; treachery and fraud vanished from sight.

units.zh: 仁壽末，授木工監，修營東都。
units.en: At the end of the Renshou era he was appointed Director of the Carpentry Office to build the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: At the end of the Renshou era he was appointed Director of the Carpentry Office to construct the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 大業初，煬帝潛有遼東意，遣弘嗣於東萊海口監造船。
units.en: At the beginning of Daye, Emperor Yang secretly planned a campaign against Liaodong and sent Hongsi to Donglai to supervise shipbuilding.
units.literal: At the beginning of Daye Emperor Yang secretly harbored designs on Liaodong and sent Hongsi to Donglai seaport to supervise shipbuilding.

units.zh: 諸州役丁苦其捶楚，官人當作，晝夜立水中，略不敢息，自腰已下無不蛆生，死者十三四。
units.en: Corvée laborers from the provinces suffered under his beatings. Officials on duty stood in water day and night without rest. Maggots bred from the waist down, and three or four in ten died.
units.literal: Corvée laborers from the various provinces suffered from his floggings; officials on duty stood in water day and night, scarcely daring to rest—from the waist down none failed to breed maggots, and three or four in ten died.

units.zh: 尋遷黃門侍郎，轉殿中少監。
units.en: He was soon promoted to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then Junior Director of the Palace.
units.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then to Junior Director of the Palace.

units.zh: 遼東之役，進位金紫光祿大夫。
units.en: During the Liaodong campaign he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
units.literal: In the Liaodong campaign he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

units.zh: 後奴賊寇隴西，詔弘嗣擊之。
units.en: Later, when slave rebels raided Longxi, he was ordered to attack them.
units.literal: Later when slave rebels raided Longxi, an edict ordered Hongsi to attack them.

units.zh: 及玄感反，弘嗣屯兵安定。
units.en: When Yang Xuan'gan rebelled, Hongsi stationed troops at Anding.
units.literal: When Xuangan rebelled, Hongsi stationed troops at Anding.

units.zh: 或告之謀應玄感，代王侑遣執送行在所。
units.en: Someone reported that he planned to join Yang Xuan'gan. Prince of Dai You had him seized and sent to the emperor's camp.
units.literal: Someone reported that he plotted to join Xuangan; the Prince of Dai, You, sent men to seize him and escort him to the imperial residence.

units.zh: 以無反釋。
units.en: He was released when no evidence of rebellion was found.
units.literal: Because there was no rebellion he was released.

units.zh: 帝疑之，除名徙日南，道死。
units.en: The emperor remained suspicious, struck his name from the rolls, and exiled him to Rinan. He died on the road.
units.literal: The emperor still suspected him, struck his name from the rolls, and exiled him to Rinan—he died on the road.

units.zh: 有子仁觀。
units.en: He had a son named Renguan.
units.literal: He had a son Renguan.

units.zh: 王文同
units.en: Wang Wentong
units.literal: Wang Wentong

units.zh: 王文同，京兆頻陽人也。
units.en: Wang Wentong was a native of Pinyang in Jingzhao.
units.literal: Wang Wentong was a man of Pinyang in Jingzhao.

units.zh: 性明辯，有幹用。
units.en: He was sharp-witted and capable.
units.literal: By nature he was clear in argument and capable in action.

units.zh: 開皇中，以軍功拜儀同，授桂州司馬。
units.en: During the Kaihuang era he was appointed Palace Attendant of the Same Rank for military merit and made military assistant of Gui Province.
units.literal: In the Kaihuang era, for military merit he was appointed Palace Attendant of the Same Rank and made Military Assistant of Guizhou.

units.zh: 煬帝嗣位，為光祿少卿。
units.en: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne he became Junior Director of the Imperial Household.
units.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne he became Junior Director of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 以忤旨，出為恆山郡贊務。
units.en: For offending the emperor he was sent out as assistant administrator of Hengshan Commandery.
units.literal: For going against the imperial will he was sent out as Assistant Administrator of Hengshan Commandery.

units.zh: 有一人豪猾，每持長吏長短，前後守令咸憚之。
units.en: A local bully held leverage over every official who came through, and successive governors and magistrates all feared him.
units.literal: There was a man bold and cunning who always held leverage over senior officials—successive governors and magistrates all feared him.

units.zh: 文同下車，聞其名而數之。
units.en: When Wentong took office he heard the man's name and rebuked him.
units.literal: When Wentong took up his post he heard the man's name and rebuked him.

units.zh: 因令剡木為大橛，埋之於庭，出尺餘，四面各埋小橛，令其人踣心於木橛上，縛四支於小橛，以棒打其背，應時潰爛。
units.en: He had a large wooden stake carved and buried in the courtyard with a foot exposed, with smaller stakes on four sides. The man was laid chest-down on the large stake with limbs bound to the smaller ones and beaten on the back until his flesh burst apart.
units.literal: He then ordered wood carved into a great stake buried in the courtyard with more than a foot exposed; on four sides smaller stakes were buried; the man was made to lie chest-down on the great stake with his four limbs bound to the small stakes, and was beaten on the back with clubs until his flesh instantly burst and rotted.

units.zh: 郡中大駭，吏人懾氣。
units.en: The whole commandery was terrified, and officials and commoners alike submitted in fear.
units.literal: The whole commandery was greatly terrified; officials and people were cowed into submission.

units.zh: 及帝征遼東，令文同巡察河北諸郡，文同見沙門齋戒菜食者，以為妖妄，皆收系之。
units.en: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong, Wentong was ordered to inspect the Hebei commanderies. He arrested all monks he found fasting and eating vegetables, deeming them deluded.
units.literal: When the emperor campaigned in Liaodong he ordered Wentong to inspect the commanderies of Hebei; Wentong saw monks observing fasts and eating vegetables and considered them deluded and false, arresting and imprisoning them all.

units.zh: 北至河間，召郡官人。
units.en: Reaching Hejian in the north, he summoned the commandery officials.
units.literal: Going north to Hejian he summoned the commandery officials.

units.zh: 小有遲違者，輒覆面於地而捶殺之。
units.en: Anyone who was slightly tardy was laid face-down and beaten to death.
units.literal: Whoever was slightly tardy or disobedient was forthwith laid face-down on the ground and beaten to death.

units.zh: 求沙門相聚講論及長老共為佛會者數百人，文同以為聚結惑眾，盡斬之。
units.en: He found several hundred monks gathered for doctrinal discussion and Buddhist assemblies. Wentong deemed this sedition and beheaded them all.
units.literal: He found several hundred monks gathered to discuss doctrine and elders jointly holding Buddhist assemblies; Wentong considered this gathering to delude the masses and beheaded them all.

units.zh: 又悉裸僧尼，驗有淫狀非童男女者數千人，復將殺之。
units.en: He also stripped all monks and nuns and examined them. Finding several thousand who were not celibate, he prepared to execute them as well.
units.literal: He also stripped all monks and nuns bare; examining them, several thousand who showed signs of licentiousness and were not celibate youths were again about to be killed.

units.zh: 郡中士女，號哭於路，諸郡驚駭，各奏其事。
units.en: Men and women of the commandery wailed in the streets. The neighboring commanderies were horrified and each memorialized the emperor.
units.literal: Men and women of the commandery wailed along the roads; the various commanderies were alarmed and terrified, each memorializing the matter.

units.zh: 帝聞大怒，遣使者違奚善意馳鎖之，斬於河間，以謝百姓。
units.en: The emperor was enraged and sent the envoy Wei Xishanyi to seize him. Wentong was beheaded at Hejian to appease the people.
units.literal: The emperor heard and was greatly enraged; he sent an envoy, Wei Xishanyi, by rapid post to chain him, and he was beheaded at Hejian to appease the people.

units.zh: 仇人剖其棺，臠其肉啖之，斯須咸盡。
units.en: His enemies opened his coffin, cut his flesh into strips, and ate it until nothing remained.
units.literal: His enemies opened his coffin, sliced his flesh, and ate it—in an instant it was all gone.

units.en: Commentary
units.literal: Commentary

units.zh: 論曰：士之立名，其途不一，或以循良進，或以嚴酷顯。
units.en: The commentary says: Gentlemen establish their reputations by different paths—some through dutiful governance, others through harsh severity.
units.literal: The commentary says: For gentlemen to establish a name, the paths are not one—they may advance through dutiful goodness, or become prominent through severity and cruelty.

units.zh: 故寬猛相資，德刑互設。
units.en: Leniency and severity must complement each other; moral teaching and punishment must work together.
units.literal: Therefore leniency and severity support one another; virtue and punishment are set in turn.

units.zh: 然不嚴而化，君子所先。
units.en: Yet gentlemen prefer transformation without harshness.
units.literal: Yet to transform without severity is what gentlemen put first.

units.zh: 于洛侯等為惡不同，同歸於酷，肆其毒螫，多行殘忍。
units.en: Yu Luohou and the others committed different crimes, yet all alike ended in cruelty, unleashing their venom and acting with savage brutality.
units.literal: Yu Luohou and the others committed different evils but alike ended in cruelty, unleashing their poisonous stings and frequently acting with savage cruelty.

units.zh: 賤人肌膚，同諸木石；
units.en: They treated human flesh as no more than wood and stone;
units.literal: They despised human flesh as no more than wood and stone;

units.zh: 輕人性命，甚於芻狗。
units.en: they valued human life less than straw dogs.
units.literal: they held human life lighter than straw dogs.

units.zh: 長惡不悛，鮮有不及。
units.en: Persisting in evil without repentance, few escaped their downfall.
units.literal: Persisting in evil without repentance, few failed to meet their downfall.

units.zh: 故或身嬰罪戮，或憂恚俱殞，異術皆斃，各其宜焉。
units.en: Some were executed for their crimes, others died of grief and rage—different ends, all meeting death as each deserved.
units.literal: Therefore some personally suffered punishment and execution, others perished together with grief and rage—different fates, all ending in death, each as was fitting.

units.zh: 凡百君子，以為有天道矣。
units.en: All men of principle took this as proof that Heaven's justice endures.
units.literal: All gentlemen of principle took this as evidence that Heaven's Way exists.
